newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end higher on strong cash.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end higher on strong cash.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed higher, with feeders posting new contract highs on demand prompted by strong cash markets, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.500 to 0.050 cent per lb higher with June up 0.475 at 65.225 cents. Feeder cattle finished up 0.750 to 0.150 with August up 0.750 at 76.475 cents. All but the January contract posted new contract highs, with May setting a new high of 73.900 and August 76.750 cents.
Rising boxed beef prices and reports that packers continued to bid for cattle Friday despite a very active feedlot trade this week prompted demand in live cattle futures, traders said.
Dan Vaught, analyst for AG Edwards, said packers were bidding steady prices for cash cattle even though they bought most of the showlists Thursday and purchased a record number in Nebraska.
"This gave the market the idea that (producers) are short bought on cattle to meet what needs they are going to have to meet (beef) features during the month of May," Vaught said.
Traders said the only resistance in futures came from continued expectations that fed cattle supplies will be rising over the next couple of months.
